t: You're standing in Berkeley Square, one of the best known garden squares in London, in the heart of Mayfair. William Kent laid it out in the mid eighteenth century. The very large plane trees in the garden were planted in 1789, and they are among the oldest in central London. Many people have been tied to the square. Charles Rolls, who went on to co-found Rolls-Royce, was born here. Poet Laureate William Whitehead died here, and so did the seventh Duke of Marlborough, grandfather of Winston Churchill. The Countess of Jersey, a noblewoman and banker, lived here.
